items.title: AI ENGINEERING ROADMAP
items.summary:
AI ENGINEERING ROADMAP
│
├── 0. Engineering Foundations (don't over-invest)
│   ├── Python done properly (type hints, async/await, Pydantic, uv)
│   ├── Git, Linux shell, Docker basics
│   ├── HTTP, REST, JSON, building APIs with FastAPI
│   ├── SQL + Postgres
│   ├── Math intuition only
│   │   ├── Vectors, dot products, matrix multiplication
│   │   ├── Probability & sampling
│   │   └── Derivatives & gradients
│   └── ★ Build: FastAPI + Postgres service, running in Docker
│
├── 1. ML Foundations (just enough)
│   ├── The training loop: data → model → loss → optimizer
│   ├── Train / validation / test splits, overfitting
│   ├── Metrics: accuracy, precision, recall, F1
│   ├── Gradient descent & backprop (do one by hand)
│   ├── PyTorch: tensors, autograd, writing a training loop
│   ├── Embeddings as a concept
│   └── ★ Build: train a small text classifier in PyTorch
│
├── 2. How LLMs Actually Work
│   ├── Tokenization (BPE) and why tokens ≠ words
│   ├── Attention & the transformer block
│   ├── Next-token prediction & sampling (temperature, top-p)
│   ├── Pretraining → SFT → RLHF / RL with verifiable rewards
│   ├── Context windows & the KV cache (why long context costs more)
│   ├── Reasoning models & test-time compute
│   ├── Why models hallucinate
│   └── ★ Build: a tiny GPT from scratch (nanoGPT-style)
│
├── 3. Building with Model APIs
│   ├── Messages, roles & system prompts
│   ├── Streaming
│   ├── Structured outputs (JSON schema → typed objects)
│   ├── Tool use / function calling
│   ├── Multimodal input (images, PDFs, audio)
│   ├── Prompt caching & batch APIs
│   ├── Token, cost & latency math
│   ├── Retries, timeouts, rate limits
│   ├── Choosing a model: frontier vs small vs open-weight
│   └── ★ Build: streaming CLI assistant with 2 tools and typed output
│
├── 4. Prompt & Context Engineering
│   ├── Clear instructions, examples, structured prompts
│   ├── Context engineering: what goes in the window, and why
│   ├── Letting the model think (reasoning, scratchpads)
│   ├── Prompt chaining & task decomposition
│   ├── Prompts as versioned code
│   └── ★ Build: 3 prompt versions for one task, compared on 30 test cases
│
├── 5. Evals (the skill that matters most)
│   ├── Why vibe-checking stops scaling
│   ├── Error analysis: read traces, label failure types
│   ├── Golden datasets built from real failures
│   ├── Code-based checks (schemas, assertions, exact match)
│   ├── LLM-as-judge, validated against human labels
│   ├── Pairwise comparisons
│   ├── Offline vs online evals
│   ├── Evals in CI as regression tests
│   └── ★ Build: eval harness for your phase 3 project; prove a change helped
│
│   ◆ CHECKPOINT 25: you can ship an LLM feature and measure it
│
├── 6. Retrieval & RAG
│   ├── When RAG beats long context (and when it doesn't)
│   ├── Embeddings & similarity search
│   ├── Chunking strategies
│   ├── pgvector first; a dedicated vector DB only when needed
│   ├── Hybrid search (BM25 + vectors) & reranking
│   ├── Query rewriting
│   ├── Retrieval evals (recall@k, MRR), separate from answer evals
│   ├── Citations & grounding
│   └── ★ Build: Q&A over a real document set, with citations and retrieval metrics
│
├── 7. Agents
│   ├── What an agent is: model + tools + loop
│   ├── Workflows vs agents (use a workflow when you can)
│   ├── Patterns
│   │   ├── Routing
│   │   ├── Parallelization
│   │   ├── Orchestrator–workers
│   │   └── Evaluator–optimizer
│   ├── Tool design (names, descriptions, error messages)
│   ├── Memory: in-context vs long-term stores
│   ├── Long tasks: compaction & sub-agents
│   ├── MCP (Model Context Protocol)
│   ├── Coding agents & computer use
│   ├── Multi-agent: when it helps vs when it just burns tokens
│   ├── Human-in-the-loop & permissions
│   ├── Agent evals: trajectory vs outcome
│   └── ★ Build: an agent with raw API calls, then rebuild it in one framework and compare
│
│   ◆ CHECKPOINT 50: you can build RAG and agents and prove they work
│
├── 8. Production AI (LLMOps)
│   ├── Serving: FastAPI + streaming to a frontend (SSE)
│   ├── Tracing & observability (OpenTelemetry + an LLM tracing tool)
│   ├── Caching (exact & semantic) and cost controls
│   ├── Model routing & fallbacks
│   ├── Latency: streaming, parallel calls, smaller models

│   ├── A/B testing prompts and models
│   ├── Feedback loop: user signals → dataset → evals

│
├── 9. AI Security
│   ├── Prompt injection (direct & indirect)

│   ├── Least privilege & sandboxing for tools
│   ├── Jailbreaks & output filtering
│   ├── OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
│   └── ★ Build: red-team your own agent and fix what breaks
│
├── 10. Open Models & Inference
│   ├── The open-weight ecosystem
│   ├── Hugging Face Transformers
│   ├── Running locally (Ollama, llama.cpp)
│   ├── Quantization (int8 / int4, GGUF, AWQ)
│   ├── Serving at scale: vLLM / SGLang, continuous batching, PagedAttention
│   ├── GPU memory math (weights + KV cache)
│   ├── Throughput vs latency trade-offs
│   └── ★ Build: serve an open model with vLLM and benchmark tokens/sec
│
│   ◆ CHECKPOINT 75: you can run, secure and self-host AI in production
│
├── 11. Fine-tuning & Post-training
│   ├── When to fine-tune (after prompting + RAG plateau, not before)
│   ├── Dataset creation & synthetic data
│   ├── SFT with LoRA / QLoRA
│   ├── Preference tuning (DPO)
│   ├── RL for LLMs: GRPO, verifiable rewards, RL environments
│   ├── Distillation: big model → small model
│   ├── Comparing against the prompted baseline
│   └── ★ Build: LoRA-tune a small model that beats a prompted one on cost or latency
│
├── 12. AI System Design
│   ├── Requirements → model choice → eval plan → architecture
│   ├── The quality / cost / latency triangle
│   ├── Build vs buy, API vs self-host
│   ├── Case studies
│   │   ├── Customer support agent
│   │   ├── RAG over company documents
│   │   ├── Coding assistant
│   │   ├── AI search engine (Perplexity-style)
│   │   ├── Voice agent
│   │   ├── Document extraction pipeline
│   │   └── LLM gateway for a company
│   └── ★ Build: written design docs for 3 case studies
│
├── 13. Specialize (pick 1–2)
│   ├── Agents & agent infrastructure
│   ├── Coding agents & dev tools
│   ├── Voice & realtime (STT → LLM → TTS)
│   ├── Multimodal & vision-language
│   ├── Document AI (OCR, extraction)
│   ├── Search & recommendations with embeddings
│   └── Inference optimization
│
└── 14. Staying Sharp & Career
    ├── Reading papers fast (abstract, figures, evals)
    ├── Testing new models on your own evals, not on launch charts
    ├── Writing up what failed and why
    ├── Portfolio: 3 deep projects > 15 tutorial clones
    ├── Interviews: AI system design, eval design, debugging a broken agent
    └── Shipping something real users touch

items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." items.title: Why is Nvidia so powerful in the AI world, and what could Jensen Huang’s scandal really cost?
items.summary:
The AI sector is notorious for the amount of circular financing going on – where companies invest in their own suppliers or customers. Nvidia is a key player in this loop.

Investors are already fretting over whether the enormous amounts of money sunk into AI can ever return profits.

While leading AI model builders Anthropic and OpenAI are moving toward public listings or fresh funding rounds, both face harsh reality checks. [...] Computer chips – specifically the chips used to produce and run artificial intelligence (AI) systems – have become a key front in the United States’ rivalry with China for geopolitical power and influence. The most powerful chips are needed for the most advanced AI, and the US has tried to maintain its edge over China by restricting access to those chips.

While the Chinese government rejects claims of espionage, Alice Huang has reportedly been under investigation by the US for years. [...] The now multi-trillion-dollar company got its start making chips called graphic processing units (GPUs), used largely for video games. However, these chips – and their successors – turned out to be ideal for the kind of number-crunching needed for training and using AI models.

Other companies such as Google and AMD have tried to make chips that can compete with Nvidia for speed and efficiency, however neither has been able to displace Nvidia from its dominance of the AI market.

items.summary:
Một số chuyên gia cho rằng các công ty trung tm dữ liệu mới nổi có thể gặp khó khăn về vốn nếu các quy định chặt chẽ hơn làm chậm tiến độ các dự án xy dựng mới. Các công ty này đã dựa vào khoản vay để mở rộng kinh doanh.

Đảng Dn chủ đã giành lại quyền kiểm soát cả hai viện Quốc hội trong cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. items.title: Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Tĩnh hướng dẫn xét công nhận sáng kiến và đánh giá hiệu quả đề tài khoa học
items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. Trong đó, giải pháp kỹ thuật có thể là sản phẩm, vật liệu, giống cy trồng, vật nuôi hoặc quy trình công nghệ; giải pháp quản lý là phương pháp tổ chức, điều hành công việc; giải pháp tác nghiệp là các phương pháp thực hiện nghiệp vụ chuyên môn; còn giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật là việc áp dụng các giải pháp kỹ thuật

items.title: Định hướng thúc đẩy ngoại giao khoa học và công nghệ
items.summary:
Để phát huy hơn nữa tiềm năng này, bà Đỗ Quỳnh Hoa cho biết, Bộ Khoa học và Công nghệ cần triển khai đồng bộ một số định hướng trọng tm. Theo đó, các hội nghị, hội thảo cần gắn với những chương trình hợp tác cụ thể, như nghiên cứu chung, chuyển giao và làm chủ công nghệ, đào tạo nhn lực, trao đổi nhà khoa học và phát triển các nhóm nghiên cứu quốc tế, nhất là trong những lĩnh vực công nghệ chiến lược và Việt Nam có nhu cầu ưu tiên. [...] Công nhn và kỹ sư Công ty cổ phần Thiết bị và Giải pháp Cơ khí Automech ở Khu công nghiệp Đình Trám (Bắc Ninh) sản xuất các thiết bị gia công cơ khí chính xác, tự động hóa. (Ảnh: TRẦN HẢI)

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Nguyên hàm của \( x^n \) (với \( n \neq -1 \)) được tính theo công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, với \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là \( \frac{x^3}{3} + C \), trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

The program currently fields Teams 26163X, 26163A, 26163L, and 26163S, providing students with opportunities to develop skills in engineering, programming, and problem-solving. [...] During the current robotics’ competition season, Team 26163X captured first place at the Tennessee State Fair Robotics Competition. The team followed that performance with another first-place finish at a competition in Elizabethton, Tennessee, where it also received a technical award recognizing excellence in robot design and engineering.

[...] DataLogix AI, a division of Trailblaze Solutions LLC, has launched online resources to help business owners explore first-person workplace video for AI and robotics training. The new resources include a workplace-video overview, an adjustable revenue calculator, a business owner guide and an inquiry form for discussing potential fit. [...] Businesses interested in learning more can use the inquiry form to describe their company and the opportunity they would like to discuss. An inquiry is not enrollment, recording permission or a payment offer. Program availability, equipment and commercial terms require separate confirmation, and payment may be zero.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
